questions.problem: What is the greatest common factor of $16$ and $24t?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the GCF, we list the factors of the coefficients and identify any common variable factors in the expressions.

The factors of $16$ are

$$
1,\,2,\,4,\,8,\,16.
$$

The factors of $24$ are

$$
1,\,2,\,3,\,4,\,6,\,8,\,12,\,24.
$$

The common factors of $16$ and $24$ are

$$
1,\,2,\,4,\,8.
$$

The greatest of these common factors is $8.$

Now we look at the variable factors. Since $16$ has no variable and $24t$ contains $t,$ there are no variable factors in common.

Thus, the greatest common factor of $16$ and $24t$ is $8.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find the GCF, we list the factors of the coefficients and identify any common variable factors in the expressions.

The factors of $10$ are

$$
1,\quad 2,\quad 5,\quad 10.
$$

The factors of $20$ are

$$
1,\quad 2,\quad 4,\quad 5,\quad 10,\quad 20.
$$

The common factors of $10$ and $20$ are

$$
1,\quad 2,\quad 5,\quad 10.
$$

The greatest of these common factors is $10.$

Now we look at the variable factors. Since $20$ has no variable and $10k$ contains $k,$ there are no variable factors in common.

Thus, $\textrm{GCF}(10k,20)=10.$
